title: लोकविश्वास र धार्मिक दर्शनमा ‘पुनर्जन्म’  {'Rebirth' in folklore and religious philosophy}
nepali: जन्म र मृत्यु प्राकृतिक घटना हुन् । पूर्वजन्म, पुनर्जन्म, स्वर्ग, आत्मा, ईश्वर, मुक्ति, मोक्ष वानिर्वाण धार्मिक सन्दर्भ र त्यसमा आधारित लोकविश्वास तथा सामाजिक आस्था हुन् । प्रामाणिक रवस्तुपरक सन्दर्भको अभाव भए पनि हिन्दू, बौद्ध, इस्लाम, ईसाई लगायतका धार्मिक ग्रन्थले कहीँ नकहीँ पुनर्जन्मलाई स्वीकार गरेका छन् । यस अध्ययनमा पुनर्जन्मप्रतिको लोकविश्वास, धर्म, संस्कारर आस्था पुस्तान्तरित चिन्तन तथा विज्ञानको प्रभावबाट केही तेजहीन बनेको अभौतिक मान्यतालाईविश्लेषण गरिएको छ । पौरस्त्य दर्शनभित्रका अवैदिक दर्शनमध्ये लोकायत÷चार्वाक दर्शनले पुनर्जन्ममाअस्वीकृति जनाएको छ भने बौद्ध दर्शनमा स्वीकृति नै देखिन्छ । जैनमा स्यादवादकै अवधारणा रहेकोछ । वर्णनात्मक तथा विश्लेषणात्मक आधारमा यस अध्ययनलाई समाजले बोकेको विश्वास र दार्शनिकविचारका आधारमा सम्पन्न गरिएको छ । यस लेखलाई पुस्तकालयीय सन्दर्भ सामग्रीको उपयोगगरी गुणात्मक अध्ययन विधिका आधारमा विश्लेषण गरेर तयार पारिएको छ । यसमा मूलतः हिन्दूलगायतका विभिन्न धार्मिक दर्शनगत विचारसँग भौतिकवादी दर्शनका विषयलाई समेट्दै पुनर्जन्म एकविश्वास मात्रै हो भन्ने निष्कर्ष पेस गरिएको छ ।
american_english: Birth and death are natural phenomena. Past life, rebirth, heaven, soul, God, liberation, moksha, or nirvana are religious contexts and the folk beliefs and social faiths based upon them. Despite the absence of authentic and objective contexts, religious scriptures including Hindu, Buddhist, Islamic, and Christian texts have acknowledged rebirth somewhere or another. In this study, folk beliefs regarding rebirth, religion, rituals, and faith, along with the non-material conviction that has been somewhat dimmed under the influence of intergenerational thinking and science, are analyzed. Among the non-Vedic philosophies within Eastern philosophy, the Lokayata/Charvaka philosophy expresses rejection of rebirth, whereas in Buddhist philosophy acceptance is evident. In Jainism, the concept of Syadvada itself is present. On descriptive and analytical grounds, this study has been conducted based on the beliefs held by society and philosophical ideas. This article has been prepared by utilizing library reference materials and analyzing them on the basis of qualitative research methods. In this, primarily incorporating the subjects of materialist philosophy alongside various religious-philosophical ideas including Hinduism, the conclusion is presented that rebirth is merely a belief.

informal_english: Birth and death are just natural phenomena, eh. Past lives, rebirth, heaven, the soul, God, liberation, moksha, or nirvana are all religious contexts and the folk beliefs and social convictions based on them. Even without proper authentic and objective evidence, religious scriptures including Hindu, Buddhist, Islamic, and Christian texts still acknowledge rebirth somewhere or another. In this study, folk beliefs about rebirth, religion, rituals, and faith, along with that non-material conviction that has lost a bit of its shine under the influence of generational thinking and science, are analysed. Among the non-Vedic philosophies within Eastern philosophy, the Lokāyata/Chārvāka philosophy rejects rebirth, whereas in Buddhist philosophy acceptance is plain to see. In Jainism, the concept of Syādvāda itself is right at the centre. On descriptive and analytical grounds, this study was carried out based on the beliefs held by society and philosophical ideas. This article was put together by using library reference materials and analysing them on the basis of qualitative research methods. In this, mainly bringing together the themes of materialist philosophy with various religious-philosophical ideas including Hinduism, the conclusion is put forward that rebirth is merely a belief.
